page.layout: Running head and page number at the top. Below them a printed ornament. Then a centred title block, theses, problem heading and question, all at full width. Below that one text column with marginal notes in the left margin, beginning with "Thesis affirm. defenditur." and "Ratio" beside the first paragraph, then I., II., III. beside its lines, and "Obiectio." beside the second paragraph. No catchword or signature.

main_text.l: METAPHYSICÆ
LIBER QUARTUS;
De Substantiis.
De substantia in genere, Cap. I.
THEOREMATA.

l.i: 1 Hactenus explicata est prima, nempe Universalis pars
Metaphysica. Sequitur altera, nempe Particularis, qua agit de
2 Eius duae sunt partes: Una, de Substantiis; altera de Ac-
3 Ens enim incomplexum aut est substantia, aut accidens.
4 Substantia est ens incomplexum, per se subsistens.

main_text.l: IN CAPUT PRIMUM
PROBLEMA I.

l.i: Utrum tractatio speciālis de ente incomplexo pertineat

main_text.l: STatuitur sententia affirmativa. Rationes sunt: 1,
Quia tractatio specialis de ente incomplexo sub ra-
tione formalem subiecti Metaphysicæ cadit, neque
eius terminos transgreditur: Siquidem in ea considera-
tur ens incomplexum, quatenus sine ullo materiæ con-
ceptu est intelligibile. 2, Quia Metaphysica est ars ca-
tholica seu universalis: Ideoque officium eius est expli-
care doctrinam generalem de substantiis & accidenti-
bus, utpote cuius usus per omnia reliquarum disciplina-
rum genera latissime est diffusus. 3, Quia omnes Philo-
sophi, qui unquam Metaphysicam conscripserunt, aut de
rebus Metaphysicis differuerunt, in eo semper consense-
runt, esse in illa disciplina de ente incomplexo in specie
agendum: Ideoque cum artificibus in sua arte sit creden-
dum, sequitur tractationem specialem de ente incomplexo
ex Metaphysicæ finibus non esse eiiciendam.
Verum contra hanc sententiam obiici possunt duo
potiffi.[?]

page.notes: The printed word "Virum" in the problem title is read as "Utrum" under the u/v rule. The final word "potiffi." is read with [?] and may be an abbreviation or a worn letter. The large initial "S" of the first paragraph is joined to the word as "STatuitur". Notes I., II., III. are placed at the approximate line where they stand; their exact position within the line is uncertain. The top right corner has a blurred shape and the bottom right shows a faint mark; these are not printed text and are left out.
